subject: Orchid Health: streaming protocol options & TTFT commitments (recap)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orchid Health: streaming protocol options & TTFT commitments (recap)

Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we aligned on and the open asks so we keep momentum toward the pilot. I pasted the raw notes below and added explicit next steps.

High-level alignment from today's call
- Goal: Replace existing sync text-generation path with a streaming-first integration for the clinical-note assistant. Pilot target traffic: ~200 concurrent sessions (peak), ~1.5k prompts/hour baseline.
- Primary performance asks: Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target: median <= 120 ms, p95 <= 400 ms (for streaming path); sustained throughput target: 250 request/s with 1–2 concurrent tokens per active stream.
- Streaming protocol: Orchid prefers SSE for ease of proxying through their infra; WebSocket OK if we need bi-directional presence. We committed to validating both in the pilot.
- Chunk cadence: client-visible chunks roughly every 100–250 ms under normal conditions; fallback to 300–500 ms during burst/batching. Typical chunk sizes: ~20–45 tokens (tokenized).
- Fallback policy: if streaming warms slowly, Redwood will automatically route to a low-latency non-streaming variant (same model family, quantized) for that request and emit telemetry for reconciliation.

Open technical validation items (we will action)
1) Pilot perf matrix: validate median/p95 TTFT on Orchid's region with their 200-concurrent profile. We attached a starter matrix (orchid_perf_matrix.xlsx) and populated baseline numbers for Redwood staging. Action: Redwood to run scheduled probe next week and share raw traces.
2) Protocol test: we will run an SSE test harness and a WebSocket test harness from Orchid's staging VPC. Need a contact for networking (NAT/proxy) tests.
3) Chunking behavior: confirm tokenization strategy and how often we emit small heartbeats vs full token chunks. We proposed initial cadence at 150 ms +/- 50 ms.
4) Observability: we will add TTFT tags to spans and emit token-level timing to your tracing. Confirm retention window for debug traces (Orchid to advise).

Next steps & owners (timeline in parentheses)
- Redwood: schedule perf probe and provide test endpoints + small test harness (by 2027-08-12) — owner: Karthik
- Orchid: provide networking contact and a staging endpoint / sample request patterns (by 2027-08-11) — owner: Elena
- Redwood Eng (Grace): prepare SSE and WebSocket harness and a short runbook describing fallback behavior (by 2027-08-13) — owner: Grace
- Redwood Sales (Ben): prepare proposed pilot contract with trial SLOs and credits for perf verification (by 2027-08-16) — owner: Ben

Attachments: orchid_perf_matrix.xlsx (initial perf grid), redwood_streaming_options.pdf (short protocol tradeoffs doc).

If that matches your recollection, we'll schedule the perf probe for Wednesday morning PST.

Thanks —
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

https://redwood.ai
From: Elena Torres <elena@orchidhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orchid Health Procurement <procurement@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 17:03:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Orchid Health: streaming protocol options & TTFT commitments (recap)

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our internal notes. A few clarifications: 

- Networking: forwarding to our infra lead, Mateo Silva (mateo.silva@orchidhealth.com). He will confirm whether we can expose a staging endpoint from our EU cluster or we'll route from US during the probe.
- TTFT bounds: our bar for go/no-go for the pilot is p95 < 500 ms. We can accept median <= 150 ms during the first 2-week run, but want to see p95 move toward 400 ms by end of pilot. Is automatic routing to non-streaming variant going to affect billing? Please call out how we'll be charged for fallback time.
- Chunk cadence: the product team prefers 200 ms nominal cadence. If you can provide a short doc of how backpressure and heartbeat tokens behave that will help our security review.

We'll aim to get networking contact to you today. Once Mateo confirms, can you send the test endpoint details?

Best,
Elena

--
Elena Torres
Director, Product — Clinical AI | Orchid Health
elena@orchidhealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Orchid Health Procurement <procurement@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchid Health: streaming protocol options & TTFT commitments (recap)

Elena — great, thank you. A couple quick answers inline and then an ask for confirmation below.

- Billing/fallbacks: fallback to the non-streaming variant will be billed at the normal per-token rate for the variant that actually served the request. For the pilot we can absorb the first 100k fallback tokens under the trial credit; anything beyond that will be billed monthly at our standard pilot rate unless you ask to pause. Ben will include this in the pilot economics doc.
- Probe location: fine if Mateo wants EU-run probes; please provide the egress IP range or a temporary SSH key for our probe runner so we can initiate from your EU cluster.
- Heartbeats/backpressure doc: attached as redwood_streaming_options.pdf — short note on how we emit heartbeats (0-length SSE events every 120 ms when no user tokens are available), and when we emit small interim token chunks. Will call out how we surface backpressure metrics in observability.

Confirm that you accept the trial SLOs defined here: median TTFT <= 150 ms for week 1, moving to <= 120 ms by week 3; p95 <= 500 ms for week 1, targeting <= 400 ms by week 3. If that's acceptable we'll schedule the probe for 2027-08-11 09:00 PDT.

Next: Ben, please circulate pilot economics and the trial SLO clause. Grace — once we have Mateo's egress details, can you and I coordinate the SSE run from their EU staging?

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchid Health: streaming protocol options & TTFT commitments (recap)

Quick internal note — prepping the SSE and WS harnesses now. A few engineering notes for the perf probe: 

- Probe config: we'll run 3 phases: warmup (5 min, 25% concurrency), ramp (15 min to target concurrency), steady (20 min at target concurrency). We'll capture per-request TTFT, token-emit cadence, and emitter-heartbeat timings.
- Instrumentation: we will tag traces with orchard_deploy=staging, probe_phase=(warmup|ramp|steady), and will provide a CSV of per-request TTFT for you to ingest.
- Chunking: default token-batching will be set to 30 tokens/emit; we will also test a 15-token low-latency mode. If network jitter exceeds 120 ms we will widen chunk cadence to 300 ms as a fallback.

Ben — I'll sync with you on the SLO wording to ensure the trial clause matches the probe plan.

Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Engineering Lead, Performance | Redwood Inference
